speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the number of requests received by the Ministry from the homeless and rough sleepers for temporary accommodation/shelters in 2021; (b) what is (i) their successful placement rates and (ii) the number of successful applicants placed on the waiting list and their estimated waiting time; and (c) what is the Ministry’s assessment, plans and alternative options for them to meet their existing and future housing needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These facilities cater to rough sleeping individuals and families with different needs and preferences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: S3Ps are set up within community premises and are operated by members of the Partners Engaging and Empowering Rough Sleepers (PEERS) Network.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The PEERS Network is a collaboration amongst community partners, social service agencies and public agencies, that join hands to support rough sleepers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: S3Ps provide rough sleepers a safe environment to rest for the night.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: MSF would refer these clients to appropriate facilities and services for further support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is no waitlist for S3Ps presently as there are sufficient spaces to support those in need of urgent shelter.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: S3Ps' schedule admissions based on S3Ps and clients’ availabilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Most applicants are admitted within three working days.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If there are no vacancies at any particular S3P at a one point of time, rough sleepers will be referred to alternative shelters or accommodation options.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Some had care needs that TSes were unable to support, such as frail seniors who required assistance with activities of daily living.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Applicants assessed as unsuitable for TS are referred to other options, for example, to Senior Group Homes which provide assisted living in public rental flats for frail seniors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Others rejected the TS option as they did not want to co-share the space with others, follow shelter rules, or to work with the social worker.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Others prefer yet to remain at familiar locations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The time taken to admit the successful applicants depends on factors such as whether the social worker is able to contact the applicants and obtain necessary information to assess their applications.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Once they are assessed to be eligible for TS, they will be offered a space.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: And for TS for individuals, there is currently no waiting list as there are sufficient spaces.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Successful applicants can be admitted immediately after the TS offers them a space.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In 2021, almost 80% of successful applicants to TS for individuals were admitted within a week.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For TS for families, there is currently no waiting list as of 12 February this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If there are families that require urgent placement such as those with children and the elderly, MSF will work with the TS operators to prioritise their admissions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For applicants who are not admitted to TS, they can stay at the S3Ps, where social service agencies and the PEERS Network will continue to engage them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For those who are not ready to seek shelter, befrienders from the PEERS Network continue to actively reach out to befriend and engage them to understand their unique circumstances and build trust with them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: When they are willing to receive assistance, befrienders help to connect them to relevant social service and Government agencies for support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: MSF and our PEERS Network partners strive to provide timely and targeted support to rough sleepers and homeless persons, including inviting more partners to join the PEERS Network and encouraging everyone to contribute to efforts to support rough sleepers and homeless persons.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If members of the public encounter any homeless individuals, they can call the ComCare hotline at 1800 222 0000, or refer them to the nearest Social Service Office or Family Service Centre for assistance.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given the delays in HDB rental flat allocations due to manpower crunch in the construction industry, has MSF observed a rise in temporary shelter requests and has coordinated upstream with HDB rental on providing shelter to those awaiting allocation?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think in the past one and a half to two years since I have joined MSF, I have been privileged to be on several night walks with our community partners and social service agencies on the ground.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: What happens on each of these night walks is that there would be MSF officers that would be tagging along the community partners, groups like those coming from the Homeless Hearts of Singapore, from the Catholic Welfare Services and together with the MSF officers is also a team of multi-agency officers as well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And one of the agencies that support the MSF officers on the ground would also be the HDB officers.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: What these means is that actually, when we encounter a rough sleeper, be it someone who is known or new to us, we will be able to very quickly pull out whatever information we may already know about this person and then make quick arrangements for this particular individual rough sleeper that we are talking about.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: What I am trying to illustrate is the fact that actually, the coordination between HDB, as well as MSF, community partners and many other agencies is right there, right from the start as we first come into contact with any rough sleeper.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And that assistance that is provided by HDB, as well as by the Government agencies and community partners, goes through and we journey with them, with each of the rough sleeper along the way.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: What probably could be better communicated to members of the public is also the fact that for rough sleepers, each of their situation is quite unique.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In my past life as a lifesaver, when I was going through training, I was always told that no two emergency incidents are the same.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think the same logic applies for rough sleepers, no two rough sleepers face the same difficulties back at home or back at their household or their families.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And sometimes, when we construe rough sleeping or homelessness as purely a single dimensional problem of housing, I think that is where we need the public mindset to slightly shift.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think we can do a little bit more in this respect.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But I assure the Member that HDB, as well as MSF and many other agencies and community partners work hand in glove to make sure that each of our rough sleepers get the customised and understanding assistance that they need.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I wonder whether the Parliamentary Secretary could share with us if the Ministry knows the exact number of rough sleepers who actually do have housing options but for various reasons, prefer to still sleep around these areas as is.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I ask this because I am sure in all our respective wards, we sometimes get feedback from concerned residents, and rightly so – why do they see this person at this place for so many days?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: They do have housing options but they prefer to rough it out and stay there.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If we all know this, I think this will allow the public to know that sometimes what they see is not a case of them having no options.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, if the Parliamentary Secretary could share with us.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Again, drawing experience from the several night walks that I have been on in the past year and a half, I have noticed exactly the same phenomenon that the Member has raised.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The fact that, sometimes alongside rough sleepers, there would be their friends who actually have homes to go back to.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: There would also be rough sleepers who actually have families to go back to, but for various reasons – it could be disputes, it could be the fact that they just want to be with their friends on the streets, it could well be that their families are living in a place that is further away and where they are rough sleeping is: number one, to be closer to their friends; and number two, perhaps closer to where they work at that particular point in time.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, for these various reasons, I think that Member has rightly pointed out that there is a small group of them that have homes to go back to, but choose not to do so for various reasons,	some of which that I have stated.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Because the assistance that each of these rough sleepers require is bespoke.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It needs to be customised to the rough sleeper's specific instance.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think the academia – NUS – has done a study in the past.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: They have a study that has recently been conducted, I think, end of last year.
